facts.text: Bacova was founded in the early 1920s by the Tidewater Hardwood Company, a Tidewater Oil subsidiary, to house sawmill workers on 40,000 acres of timberland.
The village was designed as a self‑contained model community, featuring 42 frame cottages, a commissary‑turned‑school, a chapel, and a power plant—all built in Colonial Revival style.
In 1957 industrialist Malcolm Hirsh bought Bacova, upgraded plumbing, raised rents to $9 a month, and began selling homes to private owners, ending company control.
Bacova sits in a valley along the Jackson River, about four miles west of Warm Springs, surrounded by the Allegheny Mountains and the George Washington National Forest.
The community’s name is a contraction of “Bath County, Virginia,” coined by company executive Clarence E. to reflect its local roots.
Bacova’s historic architecture and rare status as a planned company town have led to a National Register nomination, highlighting its industrial and community planning significance.
